title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — Acts 1:21 Hebraism of going in/out, not birth
pass_a_gloss: Acts 1:21 is wrongly praised: going in and out is a Hebraism for conversation and the discharge of public or private offices—not birth or death. See Beza's Annot. on the place.
pass_b_english: The place Acts 1. 21. is wrongly praised: for to go in and to go out is a Hebraism, signifying neither birth nor death, but conversation, and the functions of either public or private offices. See Beza's Annot. on that place.
source_text: Perperam laudatur locus Act. 1. 21. nam ingredi & egredi Hebraismus est, neque nativitatem neque mortem significans, sed conversationem, & vel publicorum vel privatorum officiorum functiones. vide Bez. Ann. in illum locum.

lemmas.gloss: to go in and to go out
